body:
## Pull request overview This PR hardens the MCP Pinot server’s default network exposure and the `read-query` SQL guardrails, addressing unsafe defaults (binding to all interfaces without auth) and insufficient SQL validation. **Changes:** - Default HTTP bind host to loopback (`127.0.0.1`) and refuse non-loopback HTTP binds unless OAuth is enabled. - Enforce single-statement, read-only `SELECT`/`WITH ... SELECT` validation in `PinotClient` before forwarding SQL to Pinot. - Update tests and documentation (README/user guide/changelog/docs site/Helm/env example) with secure exposure guidance and revised query behavior. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 17 out of 17 changed files in this pull request and generated 6 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | user_guide.md | Updates troubleshooting/query-error guidance to reflect stricter read-query validation. | | tests/test_server.py | Adds loopback detection tests and fail-closed startup tests for unsafe HTTP binds. | | tests/test_pinot_client.py | Adds unit tests for new read-only SQL validation behaviors. | | tests/test_config.py | Updates expectations for loopback default host. | | tests/mocks/pinot_client.py | Aligns mock error messages with new read-query wording. | | tests/mocks/execute_query.py | Aligns mock error messages with new read-query wording. | | README.md | Documents read-only enforcement and safer exposure defaults/requirements. | | PR_DESCRIPTION.md | Updates documented env examples for safer host binding and OAuth requirement notes. | | mcp_pinot/server.py | Adds loopback detection + startup refusal logic for unsafe HTTP exposure. | | mcp_pinot/prompts.py | Clarifies `read-query` as “one read-only SELECT” in the prompt text. | | mcp_pinot/pinot_client.py | Implements comment stripping, statement splitting, and read-only validation; applies it in `execute_query`. | | mcp_pinot/config.py | Changes server default host to `127.0.0.1`. | | helm/README.md | Adds Helm exposure guidance around loopback default and OAuth requirement. | | helm/mcp-pinot/values.yaml | Defaults Helm bind host to `127.0.0.1` and annotates OAuth requirement for non-loopback binds. | | docs/index.html | Updates docs-site default `MCP_HOST` value to `127.0.0.1`. | | CHANGELOG.md | Notes security hardening and updates default host in env var examples. | | .env.example | Updates default `MCP_HOST` and clarifies OAuth exposure guidance. |

issue.title: feat(auth): static shared-token auth provider for service-to-service callers
issue.body:
## What

Adds a built-in `static` auth provider alongside `none` / `oauth`.

- `AUTH_PROVIDER=static` + `MCP_STATIC_TOKEN=<secret>` → a trusted backend caller presents the secret as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Wraps FastMCP's `StaticTokenVerifier`.
- Missing/blank `MCP_STATIC_TOKEN` **raises at startup** — a misconfigured deployment fails loudly instead of booting unauthenticated.

## Why

The GHSA-73cv hardening (PR #95) makes the server refuse non-loopback HTTP binds without an auth provider. The only real provider was `oauth` (interactive OIDC/browser flow) — unsuitable for a **headless service caller** like the Cosmiq agent, which has no user in the loop and can't complete an authorization_code flow. The `static` provider is the standard service-to-service answer: a shared secret held by the caller.

This gates *access to the MCP server*; the MCP still queries Pinot with its own credentials, so it does not scope Pinot data per end user (a per-user delegated provider remains available via the entry-point seam).

## Tests
- 5 new tests in `tests/test_auth.py`.
- Full suite: **210 passed, 7 skipped**; `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean.

## Docs
- `.env.example`, README env table + the two boot-refusal notes, CHANGELOG.
